q: Everyone says just focus on taking care of yourself and the baby, dont get stressed out.
cx: At 33 weeks, moving house while her husband cares full-time for his father.

q: I feel so entitled for feeling this way but I thought pregnancy would be the ONE time in my life I could be selfish and it just hasnt happened.
cx: First baby after 12 years together; no family support and a husband with no capacity.

q: my therapist literally just nods along and says thats valid so I cancelled our appointments.
cx: Why she stopped therapy during pregnancy.

q: it is literally another full-time job for my partner to manage talking w the state, insurance, doctors, etc. We are truly so failed in the US for any kind of health care
cx: Considering respite care for her father-in-law after the baby comes.

q: I keep hearing the 16 week mark is usually when women starts to feel better. I definitely thought at 12 weeks I would feel differently which has been disappointing!
cx: At 12 weeks, sickness returned after she thought it had passed.

cx: Last-minute panic before a planned birth.

q: I don’t have one midwife though I always have someone different at my appointments
cx: Told to contact her midwife about a request; NHS, 26 weeks.

q: I wish I brought it up last week at my 25 week appointment but I didn’t so here we are. My next appointment with a midwife is at 28 weeks.
cx: First-time mother wondering if it is too late to ask for an elective caesarean.

q: This morning, I only made it to the end of my street before having to turn back home and I’m now feeling like such a failure.
cx: 27 weeks, tailbone and hip pain, trying to make her one office day.

q: my manager has mentioned in passing that some of the senior management are a bit old school and would prefer seeing people in the office.
cx: New in the job; manager supportive of working from home.

q: I think what I’m struggling a lot with, more so than the physical pain, is the immense guilt and feeling like I’m a wuss!
cx: Considering a formal request to work fully from home.

q: I’m not from the UK and back home pregnancy rights and protections aren’t as good as they are here, so you just had to grind through it.
cx: Why asking for adjustments feels like taking advantage.

q: We’re a small company and OH assessment hasn’t been raised as a possibility when they first told me to let them know if I needed any additional support.
cx: Small UK employer; occupational health never offered.

q: I thought it was a lot to ask for since I’m only in once a week and will be off on mat leave in July.
cx: Why she never asked for a standing desk at work.

q: my due date is Thursday and I have zero signs of labour. Already cried 3 times this morning because I’m so miserable! I’m bored out of my mind
cx: At 39+4, stopped the gym at 38 weeks from exhaustion.

q: I know the signs don’t really mean anything but I think it would help me feel like I won’t be pregnant forever 😂
cx: Replying to a story about late labour signs.

q: I'm mostly looking for advice and stories from first time mums who chose to do a home birth?
cx: UK, 30 weeks, preparing with hypnobirthing, weighing home, midwife-led unit or hospital.

q: I am planning a non medicated delivery anyway and have been preparing with hypnobirthing techniques since I found out I was pregnant.
cx: First pregnancy, UK.

q: I have no intention of going into this with blindfolds on, and these are very real situations that can occur - even with low risk pregnancies
cx: Thanking commenters who listed what can go wrong at home.

q: I suspect it will not be a fairy tale but as you say, it might make it feel a bit better being at home where I feel the most relaxed and comfortable.
cx: Replying to a home-birth story.

q: what are the risks of me telling my job early (note that we've had some layoffs so idk how that'd play a role too)?
cx: Seven weeks pregnant with a toddler, just given a big work event to organise.

q: The only restful sleep I've been able to have feels like it's between 6 and 7:30, when my toddler wakes up.
cx: First-trimester insomnia with a toddler.

q: given how early I am, I dont think I can tell my colleagues who are going to start to notice my lack of attention
cx: Hiding first-trimester exhaustion at work.

q: My total birth fee to my doctor was $1746 and it was due to my doctor at my 20 week appointment. I had to pay at least some of it or they wasn’t going to see me and check on my baby.
cx: First pregnancy, US, explaining why she is out of money.

q: So I had to use all $781 of my money to pay it and now I have nothing.
cx: Partner's share of the birth fee went on a water bill instead.

q: Yes I have paid maternity leave from my job. And no daycare we already have a plan with family to watch him while we work.
cx: Answering commenters who doubted she could afford the baby.

q: I have friends even my manger asking if they can come see my baby when he’s born , I’m about 2-3 months away from my due date and I haven’t gotten a thing from them , not diapers , nothing .
cx: No shower because of stress and cost; family abroad.

q: I didn’t have a baby shower because I find it’s too stressful and expensive . Why spend money on a baby shower when I can spend it on getting my baby things
cx: Explaining her visitor rule.
